mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 6%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production and employment indicate strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher when both series increase, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle signals tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher with GDP growth, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real estate investment signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher when HOUST exceeds 1200, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth combined with low federal funds rate indicates strong demand and easy policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher with both conditions, or Rank IC < 0.03.
